newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Airport Authority finding right notes.
newsitem.headline: Airport Authority finding right notes.

text.p: Hong Kong's Airport Authority looks set to follow the trail blazed by the Mass Transit Railway Corp (MTRC) and raise cash through issuing notes.
The authority said it is in the final legal documentation stages of establishing a note-issuance programme to be arranged and operated by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA).

The HKMA, also arranger and operator of a note-issuance facility of the MTRC, is keen to see issues by top Hong Kong credits like the MTRC and the Airport Authority to set another benchmark in the Hong Kong dollar debt market.
The Airport Authority facility is expected to be for HK$5 billion, but it can be increased with the agreement of the HKMA.
"This programme will become a key domestic source of the authority's long-term fixed interest rate funding," it said.
The Hong Kong market, however, languished, bankers said.

They said they were preparing for the June 30 half-year end and for the handover -- the markets will be closed on June 30 and July 1 and 2 to mark the handover, which makes Friday the last possible trading day for almost a week.
Those deals not already finalised were likely to have to wait until early to mid-July, they said.
China Travel Services Holdings Hong Kong Ltd mandated five banks to arrange a US$150 million five-year facility.
The arrangers are Bankers Trust, Banque Indosuez, LTCB, Sanwa Bank and Sumitomo Bank.
For the first three years of the facility, it is a US commercial paper programme/revolving credit facility combined, changing to a term loan for the last two years.
In other news, Thai Farmers Bank is borrowing US$150 million through a floating-rate certificate of deposit (FRCD) issue.
Issue price is par and the FRCDs are priced to float at 35 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate.
The all-in to top-tier lenders is 42 basis point, more generous than the relatively meagre 27 basis points all-in paid by another five-year FRCD in January from Thai Farmers Bank.
Siam Comercial Bank's US$100 million FRCD offered an all-in yield of 43 basis points, and earlier this month Krung Thai Bank's issue offered a 42 basis point all-in.
